finding: A round whose only finding is severity-less AND resolved wontfix/duplicate satisfies TWO conflicting predicates at once: it has 'zero surviving findings' (the wontfix finding is excluded from the surviving set), which §3.4 declares 'a separate, clean case ... independent of the severity-less fallback'; but it is also 'a non-empty panel showing no severity', which §3.4 says '--record computes ... as not-clean'. The zero-surviving clean sentence also silently conflates two different concepts — its opening words are 'zero surviving findings' but its conclusion is stated for an 'empty-panel round' (zero findings at all). --status further reads the persisted flag as the fallback 'when a round carries no per-finding severity', which this round is, yielding not-clean, contradicting the zero-surviving=clean claim. Two engineers write opposite pass/fail assertions for this reachable state.
suggestion: Pin an explicit precedence: state that the zero-surviving-findings clean case is evaluated on the surviving set BEFORE the severity-less fallback, so a round with zero surviving findings is clean even when its (all-resolved) findings carry no severity; and reserve the severity-less not-clean rule for rounds with at least one *surviving* severity-less finding. Replace 'empty-panel round' with 'zero-surviving-findings round' so the concept is consistent.

finding: Three sections promise that `--verify` discoverability is documented adjacent to `--resolve`: Overview row 5 ("`--resolve-all`/`--verify` documented adjacent to `--resolve`"), Principle 6/§2.6 ("the discoverability of `--resolve-all`/`--verify` lives in the docs adjacent to `--resolve` (§8.3, §9)"), and §8.1 (same, citing §8.3, §9). But the normative delivery sections cover only `--resolve-all`: §8.3 is titled "`--resolve-all` is documented where `--resolve` is" and its body never mentions `--verify`; §9.1 says "document `--resolve-all` adjacent to `--resolve`"; §9.3 lists "...next_action, and `--resolve-all`" with no `--verify`; and Test 15 verifies only `--resolve-all` adjacency. The `--verify` half of the promise has no section that prescribes where it is documented and no test that checks it — a section-against-section inconsistency in the modified §8 and Overview.
suggestion: Either (a) drop `--verify` from the Overview row 5 / §2.6 / §8.1 discoverability promise, since `--verify` is a review mode rather than a resolution command and its natural home is the general command docs, not adjacent to `--resolve`; or (b) extend §8.3, §9.1/§9.3, and Test 15 to also prescribe and verify `--verify`'s documentation placement, so the promise is delivered.

finding: The next_action directive/command strings embed angle-bracket placeholders — 'tp import <base>.tasks.json' (branch 1), 'tp review|audit <spec> --record <file>' (branch 4), 'tp set --workflow checks=[…]' (branch 3) — but the spec never states whether next_action emits these literally or with the placeholders resolved. §8.1 calls it 'a runnable tp command', implying substitution, yet tp cannot know '<file>' at --status time (the operator names the findings file at --record). Test 14 asserts the emitted next_action strings verbatim, so an engineer cannot write a deterministic assertion without knowing whether the output contains a literal '<file>'/'<spec>'/'<base>' or a resolved value.
suggestion: State exactly which tokens next_action resolves and which stay literal placeholders: e.g. '<spec>' resolves to the spec path, '<base>' to the spec base name, and '<file>' stays a literal placeholder because tp cannot know the operator's chosen filename. Give one fully-worked emitted example per branch so Test 14 has a byte-exact expected string.

finding: §11 systematically tests the two new exit-2 usage errors this release adds — Test 17 (invalid `review_converge_on` in the winning layer) and Test 21 (`--record` rejecting `fixed` rows) — but has no test for the third new exit-2 usage error, §6.2's rule that supplying `--harness-note` without `--record` is a usage error (exit 2) with a hint that it requires `--record`. Tests 10 and 11 cover the harness note's happy path and staleness but not the standalone-flag rejection, leaving one of the release's three new usage-error behaviors unpinned while the other two are.
suggestion: Add a §11 acceptance item: `tp review <spec> --harness-note "<text>"` without `--record` (and the `tp audit` equivalent) exits 2 as a usage error with a hint that `--harness-note` requires `--record` (§6.2).

finding: The round-7 addition to §6.3 states review and audit both surface harness_note/harness_stale "symmetrically" and defines harness_stale over "the two most recently recorded rounds," but never says whether that two-round comparison is scoped per phase (tp review --status compares only review-recorded rounds; tp audit --status only audit-recorded rounds) or globally across the whole .tp-review/ round sequence. If review and audit rounds live in one recorded sequence, a global 'two most recent' comparison would pit a review round's note against an adjacent audit round's note and raise a spurious harness_stale (or suppress a real one). An implementer must guess the scoping to build the harness_stale predicate.
suggestion: State explicitly that on tp review --status the two-round harness comparison is over review-recorded rounds only, and on tp audit --status over audit-recorded rounds only — each phase keeps its own note history — so harness_stale never compares a review round's note against an audit round's.

finding: harness_stale is 'true only when the two most recently recorded rounds both carry non-empty notes that differ', and Test 11 asserts on 'non-empty differing notes', but neither pins the comparison: (a) is 'differ' a byte-exact inequality or a whitespace/case-normalized one — is note 'x' vs 'x ' (trailing space) a difference? and (b) is a whitespace-only note (e.g. ' ') 'non-empty', or does it count as an 'empty note / no-signal'? §6.2 records anything not omitted, so ' ' IS stored, leaving its emptiness undefined. Two engineers write contradictory tests for the trailing-whitespace and whitespace-only cases.
suggestion: State that notes are compared byte-exact (consistent with 'stored verbatim'), and define 'non-empty' precisely — either the raw string is non-empty, or it is non-empty after trimming — so the whitespace-only note's harness_stale contribution is deterministic.
